translations.text: The book of the words of Tobit, son of Tobiel, son of Ananiel, son of Anauel, son of Gabael, a descendant of Sasiel, of the tribe of Naphtali.
Who was taken captive in the days of Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, from Thisbe, which is on the right-hand side of Naphtali in Galilee, above Asher.

I, Tobit, walked in the ways of truth and righteousness all the days of my life, and I performed many acts of charity for my brothers and my people who were with me in the land of the Assyrians, in Nineveh.

When I was in my own region, in the land of Israel, while I was still a child, the whole tribe of Naphtali, my ancestor, turned away and withdrew from the temple in Jerusalem, which had been chosen from among all the tribes of Israel for all the clans to offer sacrifices. The temple was consecrated as the dwelling of the Most High and was built to stand for all eternity.
And all the tribes that had rebelled sacrificed to Baal’s heifer, as did the house of Naphtali, my ancestor.

I alone often went to Jerusalem for the annual festivals, as an everlasting commandment prescribed for all Israel, bringing the firstfruits, the tithes of the produce, and the offerings they had. I gave these to the priests, the sons of Aaron, before the altar, from all the produce. And I gave the tithes to the sons of Levi who served in Jerusalem.
I gathered the second tithe and sold it, and each year I went and spent all of it in Jerusalem.
I gave the third tithe to those entitled to it, as Deborah, my father’s mother, had commanded, because I had been left an orphan by my father.
When I became a man, I took a wife from the descendants of my ancestors, and by her I fathered Tobias.
When I was taken captive to Nineveh, all my brothers and my people ate the food of the Gentiles.
But I kept myself from eating it, because I remembered God with all my soul.
The Most High granted me favor and good standing before Shalmaneser, and I was his merchant.
I traveled to Media, and I deposited ten talents of silver with Gabael, the brother of Guri, at Rages in the land of Media.
When Shalmaneser died and his son Sennacherib reigned in his place, there was unrest during his reign, and I could not travel to the land of Media.
In the days of Shalmaneser, I performed many acts of charity for my brothers.

I gave my bread to the hungry and my clothing to the naked. Whenever I saw someone from my people who had died and had been thrown outside the wall, I buried him. And if King Sennacherib killed anyone,
when he returned as a fugitive from Judea, I secretly took their bodies and buried them, because he killed many in his anger. Afterward he searched for the dead bodies but did not find them.

One of the people of Nineveh came and informed the king that I was burying the bodies, and I hid. When I learned that they were seeking to kill me, I fled in fear and went away. All my possessions were seized,
and nothing at all remained except my wife and Tobias my son.

Not fifty days had passed before his two sons killed him and fled to the mountains of Armenia. His son Esarhaddon reigned in his place, and he appointed Ahikar, the son of my brother Anael, over all the officials of his kingdom and over his entire household. And Ahikar pleaded with the king on my behalf.

And they came to bring me back, and I returned to Nineveh. Ahikar was the chief cupbearer, and all the accounts of what went out of and came into the king’s household were in his hands. Esarhaddon appointed them second to himself, and Ahikar was my nephew. When I came to my house, they restored to me Anna my wife and Tobias my son.
At the great festival, which is the holy festival of the seventh week, they prepared a great meal for me, and I sat down to eat and drink.
I saw many dishes before me, and I said to my son, “Go and bring whichever poor person you find among our brothers, and I will wait for you.”
He came and said, “Father, someone from our people, whose feet have been cast off and whose toes have fallen off, is lying dead there in the square.”
Before I had tasted anything, I went, picked him up, and brought him into my house until the sun had set.
In the evening I washed and ate my bread in sorrow.
I remembered the prophecy of Amos, as he said, “Your annual festivals will turn into mourning, and all your rejoicing into sorrow.” And I wept bitterly.
When the sun set, I dug a grave and buried him.
My neighbors mocked me and said, “Is he still not afraid of dying because of these things? Has he come back and begun burying corpses again—the very thing for which he was persecuted?”
That same night I returned after they had buried him.
I lay down to sleep, still unclean, beside the courtyard wall, and I did not cover my face.

I did not know that sparrows were perched on the roof there. I looked upward with my eyes open, and the young birds dropped their hot droppings into my eyes. I went to physicians, but they did nothing to help me. Ahikar supported me from his own pay until I went to Elymais.
My wife spun and worked with her hands and delivered her work to her employers.
They paid her wages and also gave her another young goat.

When she came to me, she began to quarrel with me, and I said to her, “Where did you bring that young goat from? Is it stolen? Give it back to its owners, for it is not lawful for me to eat anything stolen.”

My wife said, “They gave it to me as a gift in addition to my wages.” But I did not believe her and kept insisting that she give it back to its owners, and I felt ashamed because of her. She said to me, “Where are your acts of mercy and your righteous deeds now? Look, they have become plain to you!”
I was grieved and wept, and I rose and stood in prayer with an angry heart.
I said, “You are righteous, Lord, and so are all your works. All your ways are mercy, and you render judgments in truth and righteousness forever.
Look upon me and remember me. Do not repay me according to my sins and my wrongdoings, or those of my fathers, who sinned before you.

For they transgressed your commandments, and you gave us over to plunder, captivity, death, and mocking reproaches among all the nations where we have been scattered. And now, Lord, your true judgments are many,
which you have carried out against me and our fathers, because we did not keep your commandments and did not walk in truth before you.

Now deal with me according to your good pleasure, and command that my spirit be taken away, so that I may be freed from my spirit and become dust. For it is better for me to die than to live this life of mine, because I have heard false reproaches, and there is great sorrow within me. Release me from my afflictions to the eternal dwelling, and do not turn your face away from me.”
For on that very same day he had heard of what had happened to Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, who was in Ecbatana in the region of Media.

For her father’s maidservants were insulting the girl, who had been given in marriage to seven men, and Asmodeus, the evil demon, had killed them before they had come together with her as husbands and wives do. The maidservants insulted her and said, “Do you not realize that you are strangling your husbands? Look, you have married seven men and have enjoyed none of them.
Why, then, do you torment us? Why did you not perish with them, so that we would never see any children of yours?”

When the girl heard this, she was deeply distressed and wanted to hang herself. But she said, “I am my father’s only child. If I do this, I will bring disgrace upon him and bring his old age down in sorrow to the realm of the dead.”
She stood in prayer by the window facing Jerusalem and said:
Blessed are you, Lord my God, and blessed is your holy and honored name forever.
“And now, Lord, I have pleaded with you with all my heart
and asked that my spirit leave my body, so that I may no longer hear these insults.
For you, Lord, know that in my virginity I am pure of every sin.

I have not defiled my name or my father’s name. I am my father’s only child, and he has no son to inherit from him, nor any close brother or nephew for whom I should keep myself as a wife. Look, my seven husbands have perished. What good is it for me to live at all? But if you do not wish me to die, Lord, look upon me and have mercy on me, so that I may no longer hear these insults.”
The prayers of both were heard before the great Raphael.

He was sent to heal them both: to peel the white film from Tobit’s eyes, and to drive Asmodeus the demon away from Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, and give her as a wife to Tobias, the son of Tobit, because Tobias was entitled to inherit her. At that same time, Tobit returned and entered his house, and Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, came down from her upper room.

On that day he remembered the silver he had deposited with Gabael in Rages, a city in the land of Media. He said to himself, “I have asked to die. Why should I not call my son Tobias and tell him everything before I die?”
He called him and said to him, “My son,
if I die, bury me. Do not dishonor or neglect your mother, but honor her all the days of your life. Do everything that pleases her, and do not grieve her.
Remember that she endured many hardships for you when you were in her womb.
When she dies, bury her beside me in the same tomb.

Remember the Lord your God all the days of your life. Do not sin or transgress his commandments, but practice righteousness throughout your life, and do not walk in the ways of injustice. For when you act truthfully, all your deeds will prosper, as will those of everyone who practices righteousness.
Give alms from your possessions, and do not be grudging when you give alms. Do not turn your face away from any poor person, and the Lord God will not turn his face away from you.
Give alms in proportion to the abundance of what you have.
If you have little, give according to that little, and do not hesitate to give alms.
For you will store up good treasure for yourself for the day of your life.
For almsgiving saves from death and prevents one from entering the darkness.
Alms are good gifts before God for everyone who gives them.

Guard yourself against sexual immorality, and take a wife from the descendants of your ancestors. Do not take a wife from a foreign people, for we are descendants of the prophets Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, our earliest ancestors. Remember, my son, that they all took wives from among their own relatives and were blessed in their children, and their descendants will inherit the earth. And you, my son, must love your relatives. Do not turn your face or your heart away from your relatives, the sons and daughters of your people, but take a wife from among them.
For pride brings destruction and great turmoil, and impurity brings deprivation and great poverty, for impurity is the mother of famine.

Do not keep your hired worker’s wages with you overnight, but pay him at once. If you serve God, he will repay you with good things. Be careful, my son, in everything you do, and be disciplined throughout your life.
Do not do to anyone what you yourself hate. Do not drink wine to drunkenness, and do not travel while drunk.
Give some of your bread to the hungry and some of your clothing to the naked, and give as charity everything you have to spare.
Spread your bread over the graves of the righteous, but do not give it to sinners.
Seek advice from everyone, and do not disregard any useful advice.

At all times bless the Lord your God, and ask him to make your paths straight and to grant success to all your plans and undertakings. For all human plans are nothing, but the Lord himself gives good counsel, and he humbles whomever he wishes, as it pleases him. And now, my son, remember all the commandments I give you; do not let them be erased from your heart.
And now I am telling you about the ten talents of silver that I deposited with Gabael, son of Gabrias, at Rages in the land of Media.
Do not be afraid, my son, because we have become very poor. Much wealth and many possessions will come to you if you fear God, keep away from every sin, and do what is pleasing in his sight.
Tobias answered him, saying, “Father, I will do everything you have commanded me.”
“But how can I obtain the silver, since I do not know the man?”
And he gave him the document belonging to the man with whom the money was deposited.
He said to him, “Find yourself a man who will go with you, and I will pay his wages while I am still alive. Then go and collect the silver.”
Tobias went to look for a hired companion, and he found the angel Raphael.
But he did not know who he was.
Tobias said to him, “Can you go with me to Rages in the land of Media, and are you familiar with those places?”
The angel said to him, “I will go with you. I know the road, and I know Gabael, our kinsman.”
Tobias said to him, “Wait here a little while, until I go in and ask my father.” He said to him, “Go, and do not delay.”

He went in and told his father, “Look, I have found a companion who will go with me.” His father said to him, “Call him to me, so that I may learn what family he belongs to and whether he can be trusted to go with you.”
He called him inside, and they greeted one another.
Tobit said to him, “Brother, which of our tribes do you belong to? Tell me.”
He said to him, “Are you asking about my ancestry, or looking for a hired man to go with your son?” Tobit said to him, “Brother, I want to know your family and your name.”
He said, “My name is Azariah, son of Ananias the great, one of your kinsmen.”

Tobit said to him, “Welcome, brother, and do not be angry with me for asking to know your family lineage. You truly are my brother, from a good and noble family. I too knew Ananias and Jathan, and the sons, and Shema, and [?], when we went together to worship in Jerusalem and to offer the firstfruits and the tithes of our produce. They did not go astray as our brothers did. You come from noble roots and a family of great men, brother.”
“But now tell me: what wages shall I give you? A drachma a day, and provisions as for my own son?”
“And I will add to your wages if you return here safely.” They agreed to do this.

Tobias said to him, “Prepare yourself for the journey, my son, and may you prosper.” The young man prepared provisions for the journey. His father said to him, “Go, my son, with this man. May God, who dwells in heaven, make your journey successful, and may his angel accompany you.”

The two of them set out together, and the young man’s dog went with them. His mother said to Tobit, weeping, “Why have you sent our child away from us? Is he not the staff of our old age, coming and going before us?”
“Let no silver be added to silver; rather, let it be exchanged for our child.”
“For what God has provided for us is enough for us.”
Tobit said to her, “Do not be sad, sister, for he will return safely, and your eyes will see him.”
“For his good angel will guide him and make his journey successful, and he will return here safely.”
Then his mother stopped weeping.
They continued on their journey and came to the Tigris River, where they rested on the bank.
The young man went down to wash at the riverbank, and a fish leaped out of the river and tried to swallow the young man.
The angel said to the young man, “Grab the fish!” The young man caught the fish and brought it onto dry land.
The angel said to him, “Cut open the fish’s belly, take out its heart, liver, and gall, and put them away carefully.”
The young man did as the angel told him. They roasted the fish and ate it. Then the two of them went on together until they came near Ecbatana.
The young man said to the angel, “Brother Azariah, why did we take out this fish’s heart, liver, and gall?”

He said to him, “As for the heart and liver, if a demon or an unclean spirit possesses someone, these should be burned to make smoke before the man or woman, and that person will no longer be possessed.”
“And as for this gall, if someone has a white film over their eyes, they are anointed with it and healed.”
And when they approached Rages,

The angel said to the young man, “Brother, today we are to stay with Raguel. He is your relative, and he has a daughter named Sarah. Shall I speak about her, so that he may give her to you as your wife?”
“For you have the right to the girl’s inheritance, and you alone belong to her family. The girl is truly good, modest, and wise. Now listen to me.”

“I will speak with the girl’s father, and when we return here from Rhages, we will celebrate your wedding. For I know that Raguel will not give her to an outsider who is not a close blood relative, according to the law of Moses, because you have a greater right than anyone else to receive the inheritance.”
Then the young man said to the angel, “Brother Azariah, this is what I have heard about the girl: she has been given to seven men, and all of them died there in the bridal chamber.”

And I am my father's only child. I am afraid that I may go in and die like the former husbands, because a demon possesses the girl and loves her. It does not approach anyone to harm them except those who approach her to take her as a wife. Now, if I do this, I am afraid that I will bring my father and mother down to their grave in grief over me, and there is no other son to bury them.
And the angel said to him, “Do you not remember your father's instructions to take a wife from your own family? Now listen to me, and she will be your wife.”
“Do not worry at all about the demon, for tonight you will take her as your wife.”
“When you enter the bridal chamber, take burning coals mixed with ashes, on which incense has been burned, and put some of the fish's heart and liver on them, and make them smoke.”
“The demon will smell it and flee, and will never return there again.”
“When you and the girl enter the room, both of you must rise and cry out to the merciful God with much weeping, and he will save you and have mercy on you.”
“For she was prepared for you from the beginning of her life, and you will save her. She will come with you to your home, and I think that you will have children by her.”
And when Tobias heard this, he felt affection for the girl, and his soul became bound to her in love.
They came to Ecbatana and entered Raguel’s house. Sarah came out to meet them and greeted them, and they greeted her. She brought them into the house.
And Raguel said to Edna his wife, “Do you see that this young man resembles Tobit, my nephew?”
Raguel asked them, “Where are you from, brothers?” And they said to him, “We are descendants of Naphtali who were taken captive to Nineveh.”
And he said to them, “Do you know Tobit, our brother?” And they said, “We know him.” And he said to them, “Is he alive and well?”
They said, “He is well and alive.” And Tobias said, “He is my father.”
And Raguel immediately rose, kissed him, and wept greatly.
And he blessed him and said to him, “Son of a good and generous man!” And when he heard that Tobit's eyes had gone blind, he wept.
And he, Edna his wife, and Sarah their daughter were saddened. And they welcomed them and gave them lodging with great joy.

And they slaughtered a ram from the flock for them, prepared it, and set many dishes before them. And Tobias said to Raphael, “Brother Azariah, now speak about what you spoke of on the road, so that it may be done.” And he addressed the matter to Raguel. And Raguel said to Tobias, “Eat, drink, and be glad, for it is fitting for you to take my child as your wife. But I tell you the truth: I gave my child to seven men, and when they were about to go in to her, they died that very night. But now, my son, be glad.”
And Tobias said, “I will taste nothing here until you settle this matter with me.”
And Raguel said, “Then take her for yourself according to the law, for you are the girl's kinsman, and she shall be yours.”
“And may the merciful God grant you success in all that is good.”

He called his daughter Sarah, took her by the hand, and gave her to Tobias in marriage. He said, “Here she is: according to the law of Moses, take her and bring her to your father.” And he blessed them.
And he called Edna his wife, and she took all the household possessions and gave them to the girl, confirmed it in a written deed, and sealed it.
And then they began to eat, drink, and rejoice.
Raguel called his wife Edna and said to her, “Sister, prepare the other room and take the girl there.”
She did as he commanded her and took her there. The girl wept, and her mother wiped away her tears.
She said to her, “Take courage, daughter. May the Lord of heaven and earth give you joy and gladness in place of this sorrow. Take courage, daughter, take courage.”
And when they had finished eating supper, they took Tobias to the girl.

And when he entered, he remembered Raphael's words. He took the incense coals mixed with ashes, placed the fish's heart and liver on them, and made them smoke. And when the demon smelled that odor, it fled to the uppermost region of Egypt.
And the angel bound it. And when the two of them got into bed,
Tobias rose from the bed and said, “Rise also, sister, and let us stand in prayer, and God will have mercy on us.” And Tobias began to pray.
And he said, “Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers, and blessed is your holy and glorious name forever. May the heavens and all your creatures bless you.

You made Adam and gave him Eve as a helper, his wife as a support for him, and from them came all the descendants of humankind. You said, ‘It is not good for the man to be alone. Let us make him a helper like himself.’
And now, Lord, I am not taking this sister of mine as my wife for sexual immorality, but in sincerity. Look, Lord.
And have mercy on me, so that we may grow old together.” And the girl said this with him. And the two slept together that night.
And Raguel went and dug a grave for him,
for he was afraid that he too might die.
And Raguel came into his house
and said to Edna, his wife, “Send one of those maidservants to see whether he is alive. If not, let us bury him, and let no one know.”
And the maidservant went in and saw that the two were sleeping.
She went out and told them that they were alive.

And Raguel blessed God and said, “Blessed are you, Lord God, with every blessing and in your glory. May all your holy ones and all your creatures bless you, and may your chosen ones bless you forever.
Blessed are you, Lord God, for you have made me glad, and what they expected did not happen to me. Instead, you have dealt with us according to your great mercy.
Blessed are you, Lord, for you have had mercy on these two only children. Show them your mercy, Lord; bring their lives to fulfillment in health and joy.”
And he ordered his servants to fill in the grave.
And he held a wedding feast for them for fourteen days.
And Raguel said to him, “I put you under oath: do not leave here until the fourteen days of this wedding feast are completed.
Then you shall take half of my possessions, and you and the girl shall go in peace to your father. And we shall receive all the rest when my wife and I die.”
And Tobias called Raphael and said to him, “Brother Azariah,
take a young man and two camels with you, and go to Gabael in Rages in Media. Bring me the silver from there, and take him with you and bring him to this wedding feast,
because Raguel swore, ‘I will not let you go.’
Now my father is counting these days, and if we delay, he will be in sorrow and great distress.”
And Raphael went and stayed with Gabael, and gave him the written bond. And he brought him the bags with their seals and handed them over to him.
And early in the morning they went to the wedding feast there. And Tobias was happy with his wife.
And Tobit, his father, was pondering in his heart every day. When the allotted days had passed and they had not come,
he said, “Perhaps Gabael has died, and no one gave him the silver, and he is unwilling to come because of shame.” And he was very sorrowful.
And his wife said to him, “The boy is lost, for he has delayed so long.”
And she began to weep and mourn for him.
And she said, “I need nothing, my child, nothing else. Why did I ever let you go, the light of my eyes?”
And Tobit said to her, “Be quiet and do not worry. He is safe.”

And she said to him, “You be quiet, and do not deceive me, for my little child is lost.” Every day she went out to the road by which they had departed. By day she ate no bread, and at night she did not cease mourning for Tobias her son, until the fourteen days of the wedding celebration were completed, during which Raguel had sworn that they should stay there.
Tobias said to Raguel, “Let me go, for my father and mother, in their anxiety, no longer expect to see me.”
And his father-in-law said to him, “Stay here with me, and I will send servants to your father, and they will tell him about you.”
And Tobias said, “No, you must let me go to my father.” And Raguel rose and gave him Sarah his wife, half of his possessions, a male servant and a female servant, livestock, and silver.
And he blessed them and sent them away, saying, “May the Lord God of heaven grant you success, my child, until I die.”
And he said to his daughter, “My child, honor your mother-in-law and your father-in-law, for now they are your father and mother, and keep away from hateful words.” And he kissed her.

And Edna said to Tobias, “Dear brother, may the Lord bring you safely to your home, and may he let me see children born to Sarah my daughter, so that I may rejoice before the Lord. And now I entrust her to you; let her be in your care. Do not cause her sorrow from now on.”
And Tobias went on his way and blessed God because he had made his journey successful. Raguel blessed his wife, and he traveled with them until they drew near to Nineveh.
And Raphael said to Tobias, “Now, brother, do you not know how you left your father?”
“Come, let us go ahead of your wife and prepare the house.”
“And take the fish’s gall in your hand.” And they went, and the dog followed them.
And Anna sat watching the road for her son, as she usually did.
And she saw him coming and said, “Look, your son is coming, and the man who went with him as his companion!”
And Raphael said, “I know that your father’s eyes will be opened.”
“Now smear the gall around his eyes. It will sting and remove the white film from his eyes, and he will see.”
And Anna ran to meet him and threw her arms around her son’s neck. She said to him, “Have I seen you, my child? Now I can die without worry.” And they both wept.
And Tobit came outside to the doorway, stumbling and falling. His son ran to him and lifted his father up and set him on his feet.
And he applied the gall to his father’s eyes and said, “Bear it, dear father, and be patient.”
And after a little while, the white films quickly peeled away and fell from his eyes.
And he saw his son and threw his arms around his neck.
And he wept and said, “Blessed are you, Lord God, and blessed is your name forever. And blessed are all your holy angels.”
“For you disciplined me and had mercy on me, so that I can see Tobias my son.” And his son went inside with joy and told his father about the great things that had happened to him in Media.
And Tobit went out joyfully to meet his daughter-in-law, blessing God at the gates of Nineveh. Those who saw him were amazed because he could see as he walked.

And Tobit gave thanks before them, telling how God had shown them mercy. And when Tobit came near his daughter-in-law, he blessed her and said, “Welcome, daughter! Blessed is God, who brought you to us, and blessed are your father and your mother.” And there was joy among all his relatives who were in Nineveh.
And they held a wedding feast for him there for seven days.
And Tobit called his son Tobias and said to him, “Now, my son, see to the wages of the man who went with you; it is right to give him something extra.”
And he said to him, “Father, I will lose nothing if I give him half of the possessions we brought back,
for he brought me back to you safe and sound, healed my wife, brought back my silver, and healed you as well.”
And the old man said, “It is right to give it to him.”
And he called the angel and said to him, “Take half of everything you brought back.”

Then he called both of them and said to them, “Bless God, give thanks to him, and give him glory. Acknowledge before all living beings what he has done for you, for it is good to bless God, exalt his name, and honorably proclaim the accounts of God’s works. Do not delay in giving thanks to him.
It is good to keep a king’s secret hidden, but to reveal God’s works with glory. Do good, and evil will not befall you.
Prayer with fasting, almsgiving, and righteousness is good. A little with righteousness is better than great wealth with injustice. It is better to give alms than to store up treasures of gold,
for almsgiving delivers from death and itself cleanses from every sin. Those who give alms and practice righteousness will be filled with life,
and those who sin are enemies of their own lives.
Now I will not hide a single thing from you, for I have already said that it is good to keep a king’s secrets hidden, but to reveal God’s works with glory.
When you and your daughter-in-law Sarah stood in prayer, I presented the remembrance of your prayers before the Holy One. And when you buried the dead, I was with you.
And when you did not hesitate to rise and leave your meal to go and bury the dead man, I did not forget you as you did good, but I was with you.
And God sent me to heal you and your daughter-in-law Sarah.
I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels who bring up and present the prayers of the saints and enter before the glory of the Holy One.”
And both of them were shaken and fell on their faces, for they were struck with great fear.
And he said to them, “Do not be afraid. Peace be with you, and bless God,
for I did not come as a favor of my own, but by the will of your God. Bless him forever.
For throughout all the days when I appeared to you, I neither ate nor drank; rather, what you saw was like a vision.
And now give thanks to your God, for I am going up to the one who sent me. Write down everything that has happened and been accomplished.”
And it was written in this book. And they saw him no more.
They gave thanks for what had happened and for the mighty works of God, and for how the angel of the Lord had appeared to them.
And Tobit wrote a prayer of rejoicing and said, “Blessed is God, who lives forever, and blessed is his kingdom,
for he strikes and shows mercy; he brings down to the realm of the dead and brings up again, and no one can escape from his hands.
Give thanks to him before the nations, children of Israel.
For he scattered us there among them. Proclaim his greatness; exalt him before all living beings, for he himself is the Lord our God, our God and Father forever and ever.
He will punish us for all our unrighteous deeds, and again he will have mercy on us and gather us from all the nations among whom we were scattered.
If you turn to him with all your heart and with all your soul, and act truthfully before him, then he will turn to you and will not hide his face from you.
You will see what they will do with you. Praise him with all your mouths, bless the Lord who is righteous, and exalt the eternal King.

In the land of my captivity I gave thanks to him, and I will show his power and greatness to sinful nations. Now turn back, you sinners, and do what is righteous before him, for who knows whether he will be pleased with you and have mercy on you?
But I will bless my God, and my soul will bless the King of heaven, and I will rejoice in his greatness.
All nations will say this, and they gave him praise in Jerusalem, in the holy city.
He will discipline the children of your people, and he will turn again and have mercy on the children of the righteous.
Give thanks to the Lord, the benefactor, and bless the eternal King, so that he may rebuild his dwelling within you with joy.
Those who are captives will rejoice in you, and those who are afflicted among all the nations will love you forever.

Many nations will come from far away in the name of the Lord God, carrying their offerings in their hands to present them to the heavenly King, and they will bring you joy from generation to generation.
May all who hate you be cursed, and may blessings come upon those who love you.
Rejoice and be glad over the children of the righteous. They will gather together and together bless the Lord of righteousness.

Blessed are those who love you; they will rejoice in your peace. Blessed are those who mourned over your destruction, for they will rejoice in you again when they see your glory, and they will be glad forever.
May my soul bless God, the great King.
For Jerusalem will be built of precious stones, of sapphire and ruby, and your walls of other precious stones as well; your towers and battlements will be of pure gold.
All the squares of Jerusalem will be adorned with crystal, malachite, and carnelian stones.
In every street of Jerusalem they will say, “Alleluia!” They will give praise and say, “Blessed is God, who has exalted the whole world forever.”
And when Tobit finished this praise,
he was fifty-eight years old when his eyes lost their sight, and after eight years his eyes were opened again.
He gave alms and continued to grow in his fear of the Lord God and in giving him praise.
He grew very old.
He called his son and his grandson and said to him, “My child, take your children, for look, I have grown old and am close to death. Now go to the land of Media, my child,

for I believe what Jonah the prophet said about Nineveh: that it will be destroyed, while there will be peace in the land of Media for a time. For our brothers will be scattered from this good land, and Jerusalem will become a ruin and a wilderness, and the house of God within it will be burned and remain in ruins for a time.”

And God will again have mercy on them and bring them back to the land, and they will build the house, though not according to its former pattern, until the times of the ages are fulfilled. After this they will return from captivity here and build Jerusalem with glory and great honor. The temple of God will be built in it for all generations forever, a glorious building, just as the prophets spoke concerning it.
And all the nations will turn to fear the Lord God in truth, and they will destroy and cast away their idols.

And all the nations will bless the Lord, and the people will give thanks to their God. The Lord will exalt his people, and all who love the Lord God in truth and righteousness will rejoice. And you must practice the charity of your fathers.
And now, my son, go away from here, for what the prophet Jonah said will surely happen.
But you must keep the laws and commandments, and be merciful and righteous, so that it may go well with you.

Bury me, and your mother with me, and remain no longer in Nineveh. My son, see what Adam did to Ahiqar, who had raised him: how he led him from light into darkness, and how much evil he inflicted on him. But Ahiqar survived, and repayment was made to him in return, and Adam went down into darkness in his place. And Manasseh performed acts of charity and survived on the day of death that had been secretly intended for him, while Adam fell into the snare and perished.

And now, my son, see what charity accomplishes and how righteousness saves. When he had said this, he gave up his spirit upon his bed, for he was one hundred and fifty years old. His son buried him with great honor, after a good end to his life.
And when Anna died, he buried her beside his father. Then Tobias went with his wife and his sons to Ecbatana in Media, to his father-in-law Raguel.
He grew old in great honor, and he buried his father-in-law and his mother-in-law with glory and honor. He inherited their house and the house of his father Tobit.
And he died at the age of one hundred and twenty-seven in Ecbatana in Media.

Before he died, he himself heard of the destruction of Nineveh, which Nebuchadnezzar Ahasuerus had captured. Before his death, Tobias rejoiced over Nineveh and gave glory and thanks to God, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen. Tobit is finished.
